text: The built-in sandbox judges a Go package's acceptance tests and existing tests from a binary built without the test files the build added, hidden by an overlay, and runs only the tests those files declare from the binary that holds them (#869). A build may add test files, and one binary held them all, so an added file could set production state as the binary started, declare a helper a pinned test called, or exit from a TestMain before a package's own tests ran: the audit passed a plan's acceptance tests with production unchanged, and switched an existing test off. A binary that doesn't build without the added files fails the check, saying which. An added Go test file that declares TestMain or init is also refused at staging and in CI's scope, since CI's go test runs every file together. The configured Go path keeps one binary until #870.
